ai.description: Nanorana rarica is a small frog (30–40 mm) with a brown, warty dorsum and yellowish belly. It is distinguished by a lack of vocal sacs and the presence of distinct, prominent black tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nanorana rarica* is best distinguished by the presence of prominent, black-tipped nuptial spines on the chest and forelimbs of males, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Nanorana rarica* inhabits high-altitude Himalayan streams and surrounding alpine meadows, typically found at elevations between 2,400 and 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Rara Paa frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky, high-altitude streams of its Himalayan habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nanorana rarica* breeds in streams during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of eggs attached to submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nanorana rarica* is endemic to the high-altitude regions of western Nepal and the adjacent Kumaon Himalayas in Uttarakhand, India, typically found above 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Rara Paa Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "peep" notes, typically heard near the edges of high-altitude streams and ponds in the Himalayas.
